## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`); a uv workspace of four packages under `packages/`.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small. About 130 quarterly files since 1993, plus one daily file per business day. Minutes of downloading at 3 requests/s. Basis: the SEC full-index and daily-index directories. Measured by Stage 1. |

## Open questions

1. **Platform.** The ADR proposes Azure (ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage). Its status is Proposed, and you named it background. Stages 1–6 run locally and do not depend on the answer. Stage 7's brainstorming settles it.
2. **Scope overlap.** Spec §2.2 puts filing-document downloads out of scope. Your progression (O2, O3) includes them. Your progression governs, and the spec remains background for O1 only. Stage 2's brainstorming settles what "submission" means: the full submission `.txt` or the filing folder's documents.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Index table, one quarter
      Objective: Ingest one real closed quarter's master index, plus the real daily indexes of the open quarter, into one queryable filing-index table.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: a local filing-index table and the code that fills it from SEC quarterly and daily index files; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — the table holds every row of both real sources, with quarterly/daily overlap deduplicated; findings record the files fetched, bytes, row counts, wall time and the observed request rate (identifying User-Agent, under the SEC ceiling).
      Leaves out: raw-snapshot manifest and replay (Stage 4); quarterly reconciliation, withdrawals and versioned publication (Stage 5); historical formats before the chosen quarter and the full 1993– backfill (Stage 6); scheduling, catch-up and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submissions for one quarter
      Objective: Download the submissions that Stage 1's closed-quarter index rows name.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table
      Produces: the submissions of one real quarter on local disk, keyed to their index rows; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-2-findings.md
      Exit: O2 — every index row of the quarter maps to a downloaded submission, or to a reported failure; findings record file count, bytes, wall time and request rate, and project the full-history duration from them.
      Leaves out: resumable checkpoints and provenance manifest (Stage 4); the full-history campaign (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick the 10-K and 8-K filings (amendments included) out of Stage 2's submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's submissions on disk
      Produces: the extracted main documents of one quarter's 10-K and 8-K filings, linked to their index rows; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-3-findings.md
      Exit: O3 — every 10-K and 8-K row of the quarter has an extracted main document, or a reported reason why not; findings record counts, failures and processing time.
      Leaves out: provenance on extracted documents (Stage 4); format coverage across the full history (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Provenance and replay
      Objective: Retain original bytes under a source manifest, so that any parser change reprocesses stored inputs without new SEC requests.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 1–3 code and outputs
      Produces: a source/snapshot manifest, content-addressed raw storage, row and document provenance, and resumable per-file checkpoints
      Exit: with SEC access disabled, a replay of Stages 1–3 from raw storage reproduces the same table and documents with no duplicates; an interrupted run resumes without refetching completed files.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Index corrections and versioned publication
      Objective: Reconcile later quarterly index changes, and publish each quarter as a complete versioned generation behind one active pointer.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 4's manifest and raw storage
      Produces: per-quarter generations, an active-pointer reader contract, change reports and gated withdrawals (background: spec §4.4, §4.6)
      Exit: a changed quarterly snapshot publishes its additions and updates; a snapshot that removes keys waits for approval; a crash mid-publish leaves the prior generation readable.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Full index history and validation suite
      Objective: Cover every historical index format with fixtures, and backfill the index table from 1993.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 4–5
      Produces: committed golden and malformed fixtures across formats, a CI suite on mocked SEC responses, and the full-history filing-index table
      Exit: CI passes without SEC access; the full backfill completes, or reports each unresolved quarter by name.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduled operation and deployment
      Objective: Run daily ingestion and reconciliation on a schedule, on the chosen platform, under one shared SEC request budget.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stage 6; Open question 1 answered
      Produces: deployed scheduled runs, catch-up after missed runs, one request budget across concurrent runs, alerts and runbooks
      Exit: observed scheduled runs ingest new daily indexes and their submissions, a deliberately missed run catches up, and concurrent runs never exceed the configured request rate.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Full-history submissions campaign
      Objective: Download and handle every historical submission as a bounded, resumable campaign alongside daily operation.
      Outcomes: O2, O3
      Consumes: Stage 7's shared budget and deployment; Stage 2 findings (duration projection)
      Produces: full-history submissions and 10-K/8-K extractions; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-8-findings.md
      Exit: every index row has a submission or a named unresolved gap; findings record actual against projected duration and bytes.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line. writing-plans copies it verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

Once every stage is ticked, re-run the gap rubric over O1–O3 against the accumulated system. Cite evidence per verdict: the implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, and `specs/deferred_items.md` entries. Each unmet outcome either becomes a new stage or is deferred with a written why.
